sentences.text:
3. Facts in brief which are necessary for disposal of present appeal are as under:
4. A claim petition came to be filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short the 'M.V. Act'), by the injured in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.06.2008 at about 10.00 p.m., involving a Tractor Trailor Unit bearing registration No.KA-27/TA-1341 and Trailor No.KA- 26/T-1598.
The injured was travelling as a coolie/hamali in the said Tractor Trailor Unit.
5. Further he had suffered the accidental injuries and treated in the hospital and discharged on 05.12.2008.
6. After discharge, he has filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
However, on account of the accidental injuries NC: 2024:KHC-D:1055 sustained by the claimant, ultimately he committed suicide and died.
7. The claim petition got amended by bringing on record the legal representatives of the deceased claimant who are the dependents of the deceased.
8. The claim petition was resisted by the Insurance Company by filing necessary written statement in respect of the amended claim petition averments.

9. The Tribunal raised following issues based on the rival contentions of the parties:
"ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, deceased sustained injuries in the accident on 08.06.2008 and died as stated in the petition?
2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?"

10. In order to prove the case of the claimant, one of the legal representatives of deceased claimant got examined as PW.1 and relied upon 16 documents which were exhibited and marked as Exs.P.1 to P.16.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1055 11.
On behalf of respondent-Insurance Company no oral evidence is adduced and on behalf of respondent one document is marked at Ex.R.1 i.e., Insurance Policy.

sentences.text: The Tribunal on cumulative consideration of the material evidence placed on record, allowed the claim petition by awarding a sum of Rs.4,93,582/- as compensation contending that there is a nexus established between the suicidal death of the claimant and the accidental injuries suffered by him and dependents are entitled for the aforesaid compensation.
13. Being aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company is in appeal.

14. Sri G.N.Raichur, learned counsel for the appellant, reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, vehemently contended that the material on record would not indicate that the death of the claimant is due to accidental injuries.
Therefore, Tribunal erred in awarding compensation to the dependents of the deceased in a sum of Rs.4,93,582/-, as referred to supra and sought for allowing the appeal.

15. He also pointed out that in such case, when the person has died, after he has been discharged, it has to be NC: 2024:KHC-D:1055 construed as natural death and therefore, claim petition ought to have been dismissed and hence, sought for allowing the appeal.

16. Per contra, Sri B.S.Sangati, learned counsel representing the claimants vehemently contended that though claimant got discharged finally on 05.12.2008 as per Ex.P.10, for the injuries sustained in by the claimant he could not attend to his day to day work and he was feeling depressed in his life.
Ultimately, on account of depression suffered by him due to accidental injuries, the injured committed suicide on 24.12.2009.
Therefore, there is sufficient nexus between the death of the claimant and accidental injuries suffered by him and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
17. In view of rival contentions, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

On such perusal of the material on record, it is pertinent to note that the original claimant-Neelappa Angaragatti being Hamali of the tractor trailor bearing registration No.KA-27/TA-1341 and KA-26/T- 1598 and suffering injuries is established by placing necessary oral and documentary evidence on record.

The medical records and police records would go to show that it is the driver of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:1055 Tractor Trailor who was responsible for negligent driving and therefore,
original claimant suffered the injuries.
18. The material on record also discloses that on 05.12.2018 original claimant has been discharged from the hospital.
Said discharge summary on perusal, would go to show that original claimant has been cured completely of all the injuries sustained by him.
19. Admittedly, the original claimant died by committing suicide on 24th December 2009.
In such circumstances, claim petition also came to be amended by impleading the legal representatives of deceased original claimant-Neelappa by amending the cause title.
20. What exactly is the reason for Neelappa to commit suicide is not forthcoming on record with any probable and cogent evidence.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, the Tribunal assuming that Neelappa died suicidal death on account of the accidental injuries suffered by him and thereby establishing the nexus of death of Neelappa with accidental injuries in the considered opinion of this Court is incorrect.
However, on that ground, the entire claim petition cannot be dismissed as is contended by learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company.

23. Sri B.S.Sangati, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2, at this juncture contended that the medical records available on record would go to show that the original claimant has spent an amount of Rs.22,582/- towards the medical bills etc.,
Admittedly, Neelappa has suffered fracture injury.
Therefore, his day to day life has been crippled to a considerable extent.
24. Therefore, a case is made out for reassessment of quantum of compensation for the accidental injuries suffered by Neelappa during his lifetime.

25. Hence, quantum of compensation is reassessed as under for the accidental injuries suffered by original claimant (injured):
Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-
Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-
Attendant, nourishment charges Rs.15,000/-
Medical bills Rs.22,582/-
 NC: 2024:KHC-D:1055 Loss of income during laid up period Rs.10,000/-
Transportation and other charges Rs.05,000/-
TOTAL Rs.1,02,582/-
 26.

Therefore, the reasoning assigned by the Tribunal that the legal representatives of the original claimant are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.4,93,582/- as dependents cannot be countenanced in law and are entitled to The Divisional Manager vs Somappa S/O. Neelappa Angaragatti on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35392920/
5 Rs.1,02,582/- as aforesaid.

27. Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) As against a sum of Rs.4,93,582/-, the legal representatives of the original claimant are entitled Rs.1,02,582/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
(iii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be  transmitted to the Tribunal for  disbursement.

Excess amount if any, is  - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:1055 ordered to be returned to the Insurance Company.
